K:heavy-light.objective: Children look at two everyday objects and circle the one that is heavier.
K:heavy-light.mistake: Children circle the thing that looks bigger. A big balloon is chosen over a small rock, because to them bigger has always meant more.
K:heavy-light.words: Bring a balloon and a rock, or a big empty box and a small full bottle: "Which is bigger? Which is heavier? Hold one in each hand." Say: "Big is how much room it takes up. Heavy is how hard it pushes down on your hand."

3:input-output.objective: Children use the rule printed on a number machine, such as + 7, − 4, or × 5, to fill in the missing numbers going in and coming out.
3:input-output.mistake: Children use the rule the same way in every row. When the number that went IN is missing, they apply the rule forward again and do not undo it: on a + 7 machine with 12 coming out they write 19, not 5; on a × 5 machine with 30 coming out they write 150, not 6. Some read a minus rule as plus.
3:input-output.words: Have children read the rule aloud first: "This machine adds 7 to every number." For a number coming out (the output): "5 goes in. Add 7. What comes out?" For a number going in (the input): "12 came out. The machine added 7. What went in? Undo it: 12 minus 7." On a times machine: "30 came out. The machine multiplied by 5. What number times 5 makes 30?" Ask: "How can you check? Put your number in and run the machine."

2:digraphs.mistake: Children find sh at the start of words and miss it in the middle and at the end (fishing, brush). Some circle every s and every h they see, even when the two letters are not side by side.
2:digraphs.watch: Compare the number in the box with the number of circles. A child who reads silently misses more; have that child whisper the sentence. Check words like "fish" and "washing," where the team is not at the start.

2:cursive-writing.title: Cursive letters and connections
2:cursive-writing.objective: Children trace and write rows of connected cursive letters (i, t, u, and w) and connect two letters without lifting the pencil (for schools that teach cursive in Grade 2).
2:cursive-writing.mistake: Children lift the pencil after every letter and add the connecting stroke afterward, so the row is print letters with tails. Some stop in the middle of a word to dot the i or cross the t, which breaks the flow.
2:cursive-writing.words: Say: "Keep the pencil down until the whole word is written. Then go back: dot the i, cross the t." Name the strokes: "up, down, and out to the next letter." For w: "W ends high, at the middle line, so the next letter starts from up there, not from the bottom line." Write it big in the air first, then on the page.
2:cursive-writing.watch: Watch the pencil, not the page: is it lifted inside a word? Check that each connection starts where the letter before it ended and that the letters sit on the line. Right-handed children tilt the paper with its top to the left; left-handed children tilt it with its top to the right, so that the hand stays below the writing.
